clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 4: the overflow fallback of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:40-52). Boundaries per price; whether a wrapped product can pass line 43; and whether a swap step can reach the fallback and return.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Read src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:40-52. With a > 0 and a*s >= 2^256 the wrapped product is a*s - k*2^256 with k >= 1, so floor(product/a) < s and line 43 rejects it; line 45 rejects a wrapped sum. The fallback at line 52 divides by floor(N/s) + a with checked addition, and floor(N/s) <= N/s makes the result round toward a higher price, which for a zeroForOne step means less movement and is in the pool's favour. SwapMath.sol:64-79 calls getNextSqrtPriceFromInput only when the amount less fee is below amountIn, so the whole remaining amount is consumed and Pool.sol:455-459 casts amountSpecified with SafeCast.toInt128 (src/libraries/SafeCast.sol toInt128(int256) reverts on y != x; the surrounding unchecked block does not reach into the library). TickBitmap.sol:85-105 keeps the target inside the current word, which for a positive start tick is at or above tick 0. I ran a read-only eth_call with a code override that computes the wrapped product, its quotient by a and the line 52 divRoundingUp for a = 2^127-12345, s = 2^129+987654321, L = 2^127-1 on MegaETH (mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc), HyperEVM (rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm), Monad (rpc.monad.xyz) and Tempo (rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz): all four returned the Python words, the quotient below s and the fallback result at most s. The Ethereum publicnode endpoint answered HTTP 403 to my request, so I did not get its answer.

clearedSpotChecks.check: clear, settleFor and ERC-6909 semantics read and run: src/PoolManager.sol:305-319, src/ERC6909.sol:25-64, src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Read src/PoolManager.sol:300-346. clear (310-319) converts amount with SafeCast.toInt128(uint256), which reverts for 2^127 or more, requires equality with the caller's own delta and only lowers that caller's delta. settleFor passes the named recipient into _settle (349-364), whose ERC-20 side reverts on msg.value > 0 at 356 and measures paid from the synced reserves, so the payer funds the credit. src/ERC6909.sol:25-48 uses checked subtraction on balances and on finite allowances, skips the allowance for the owner and operators and leaves type(uint256).max allowances unchanged; src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22 applies the same rule to burn. I found no path where one account lowers another's claims or deltas without that account's allowance or operator grant. compare.json shows no word difference outside cases 1191 to 1193 on any of the 21 networks.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 1 coverage: which of the 117 branch sides that cycle 24 lists as never executed by the MegaETH, Monad or HyperEVM producers ran in these cases (pyevm_cov counters on the PoolManager code).
clearedSpotChecks.note: The four sides left out match the code: src/PoolManager.sol:181 runs only with a non-zero hookDelta from a hook with return-delta flags (pool-creator), src/PoolManager.sol:356 is the NonzeroNativeValue revert for value sent while an ERC-20 is synced, and src/types/Currency.sol:48-51 is the native payout call and its revert. The last two are revert sides, so a wrong answer there could only make a call revert or not revert; the :356 side would need a producer that skips the revert to credit msg.value as a token. That remains unobserved on the closed producers of MegaETH and HyperEVM, which is the research's own low priority lead. In compare.json the extra differences against Ethereum on MegaETH (case 1192) and Tempo (case 1193) are gas outcomes: Ethereum also fails case 1193 at the unlock frame, and Tempo completes it. The research text names the MegaETH unlock-frame failures but not Ethereum's own unlock-frame failure on case 1193; this does not change the result.
